must_identify: isRecurring is not merely a visual toggle here: it selects two stable identities with different invariants, required inputs, save contracts, consumers, and change axes.
The optional-prop surface permits invalid combinations and forces non-null assertions because the component contract does not encode either workflow cleanly.
The split is justified by independent business contracts and ownership, not by a mechanical rule that every render branch deserves a component.
acceptable: Expose SingleAppointmentEditor and RecurringSeriesEditor with focused required props, optionally retaining a thin routing wrapper when a caller genuinely needs it.
Use an explicit discriminated union when one public entry point is valuable, while still delegating the two workflows to clear internal owners.
Keep small shared display primitives below the two workflow components without forcing their business contracts back together.
must_not: State that any boolean prop or any render branch automatically requires a component split.
Preserve one bag of optional props and rely on non-null assertions as the contract.
Treat this as an Effect, memoization, closure, ref, or other React runtime issue.
Introduce a config-driven renderer to encode both flows.
